Part · Getting started

What the jet is, how to install it, how to start it.

1. About this manual and the jet

This is a plain-language guide to the F-15EX V3 mod: what is in the cockpit, what each picture on every screen means, and how to do the common jobs (start up, find a target, shoot, defend yourself, navigate, land). It covers all three jets: the F-15EX, the F-15EX (CFTs) and the F-15IA.

The pictures in this manual are drawn by the mod's own display code, so the symbols are exactly what you will see. The numbers in them are only examples (a 29,800 ft altitude, a 654 kt airspeed and so on) so that every symbol shows up at the same time.

Controls are named in this manual exactly as they appear in DCS under Options → Controls, for example MASTER MODE - A/A. Search for the name in the Controls list to find or change its key or button.

Note. Some screens follow the real jet's pictures closely; some are the mod's own design where nothing public exists (the A/P page, KEY PAD, CMD programs, INS page, the TF, IFF and LINK 16 pages, and parts of FCS and BIT). Those are marked own design where it matters.

What is new compared with the F-15EX V2.33 mod

  • Own flight model. F110-GE-129 engines, real fuel (13,550 lb internal; 23,305 lb with CFTs), fly-by-wire with G and angle-of-attack limiting (30° AoA, 25° on the CFT jets), new landing gear, brakes and nosewheel steering.
  • Own cockpit. HUD, helmet display (HMD), a large touchscreen (LAD), engine/fuel display, standby display, RWR page, radios, IFF, autopilot with terrain following, INS and navigation, cold start and electrical system, exterior lights.
  • AN/APG-82(V)X style AESA radar with track-while-scan, AIM-120 guidance, target recognition (NCTR) and a low-probability-of-intercept search that other aircraft's warning receivers do not hear.
  • Datalink picture from friendly AWACS, ground radars and fighters, in single player and multiplayer.
  • Weapons: AIM-120C-5/C-7/C-8/D/D-3, AIM-174B, AIM-260A, AIM-200A, AIM-9X, APKWS against drones, the M61 gun, and any other air-to-air missile you add yourself. Air-to-ground weapons are not part of this release.
  • Missile countdown: after a launch the ATTACK line and the HUD show time to impact (T) and time to active (A / ACT).
  • Auto GCAS: if the jet is going to fly into the ground it rolls level and pulls up by itself; the paddle takes control back.
  • Defence: RWR/TEWS page, chaff/flares with editable programs, voice warnings, low-altitude and pull-up warnings.

2. Install, update and set up your controls

Install

  1. Close DCS. Remove any older F-15EX mod folder from Saved Games\DCS\Mods\aircraft (for example F-15EX V2.33). Only one F-15EX mod can be installed at a time.
  2. Copy the Mods and Scripts folders from the package into Saved Games\DCS, merging them with the folders already there.
  3. Keep the mod folder's name, F-15EX V3: the helmet hook finds the mod by that name.
  4. Start DCS. The jets appear as F-15EX (after the model app below), F-15EX (CFTs) and F-15IA in the mission editor.

Build the external model (the CFT app)

This release ships no external 3D model and no model LOD tables. The F-15E CFT Removal app in the package's Tools folder writes both LOD tables and builds both models from the model file you choose:

  1. Run Tools\F-15E CFT Removal\F-15E CFT Removal.exe.
  2. Step 1: choose the external model file you want to use.
  3. Step 2: choose the mod folder, Saved Games\DCS\Mods\aircraft\F-15EX V3 (the folder that holds entry.lua).
  4. Step 3: press Build and install. It writes Shapes\F15EX.lods and Shapes\F-15EX.lods, Shapes\F-15EX_CFT.edm (CFT / F15IA) and Shapes\F-15EX.edm (CFT-free), and enables the non-CFT F-15EX. Start DCS afterwards.

Until the app has run, the F-15EX variant is not offered and the CFT jets have no external model. The app never writes into the DCS install folder; it keeps the previous model as a .bak file beside the new one.

The package puts two files into Saved Games\DCS\Scripts\Hooks:

FileWhat it doesWithout it
F15EX_HMD_hook.luaFeeds your head position to the helmet display and the mission's unit data to the radar and datalink.The helmet symbols stay fixed to the nose; friendly datalink aircraft show no type.
F15EX_DL_relay_hook.luaMultiplayer: passes friendly AI fighters' datalink tracks from the server to you.In multiplayer you still get AWACS tracks and friendly positions, but not the AI fighters' tracks.

Multiplayer servers

Friendly AI fighters' datalink tracks are made on the server, so the server passes them on to F-15EX players of the same coalition over its own TCP port (default 10320).

  • On the server (dedicated or hosting), install the mod and both hooks into the server's Saved Games folder, and allow TCP port 10320 in through its firewall and router.
  • Each F-15EX player gets one chat line naming the server's address when the relay connects.
  • To change the port or to give the server's public address, add these lines to Mods\aircraft\F-15EX V3\bin\F15EX_MslLink.cfg on the server (create the file if it is missing): dl_relay_port=10320 and dl_relay_addr=your.public.address.

Updating from an earlier version

  1. Close DCS. Delete the old F-15EX folder completely (do not copy over it), then add the new one with the same folder name.
  2. Check that both hook files are still in Scripts\Hooks.
  3. Missions made with the V2.x loadouts: the old loadout IDs load as empty pylons with no warning. Open the aircraft in the mission editor and choose a V3 preset (26 per variant), or load the stations by hand.

Setting up your controls

  • The jet's own controls are in the categories ending in (EX) (AUTOPILOT, DISPLAYS, NAV, NVG / HMD, RADIOS, SYSTEMS, TEWS, WEAPONS) and in RADAR. Some general ones (gear, lights, brakes, nosewheel steering) are in Systems.
  • A few old FC3 entries still appear in the list (in categories such as Sensors and Modes). They do nothing in this jet.
  • Most commands have no joystick default: bind them to your HOTAS yourself. Chapter 13 lists every control name.
  • Worth binding first: the TDC (four directions), the four TMS directions, the four castle directions, chaff, flare, CMD MAN 1 and MAN 2, master mode A/A and NAV, weapon select, master arm, weapon release, gun trigger, the AIM-9X uncage and the NWS button.
Tip. If an extra missile you added is missing in the mission editor, open the dcs.log: the mod writes one line per jet when it adds the missile list (it contains ANY).

Reporting a problem

Right after the flight, before starting DCS again (DCS overwrites it), send Saved Games\DCS\Logs\dcs.log and the track file (.trk) of the flight, and say which jet, which mission, and roughly when in the flight it happened. The mod itself writes no log files.

3. Quick start: from cold to airborne

On a cold jet the displays are off. The cockpit follows a real start order, but you can let the jet do it for you.

Automatic start

Use ENGINE - Auto start (again: cancel). The jet starts itself, including aligning the INS. Use it again to cancel.

By hand (about one minute)

  1. ELEC - Battery ON / OFF: battery on. The engine display (EMD) and standby display come up first.
  2. JFS - Start / off: start the jet fuel starter. Wait until the caution list says JFS RUNNING. The HUD and LAD come up now (battery plus JFS is enough; you do not need a generator).
  3. Both throttles to IDLE with ENGINE - Right throttle OFF / IDLE and ENGINE - Left throttle OFF / IDLE. The right engine cranks first and lights at about 18 % RPM, then the left. The EMD shows the RPM from 1 %, and the amber OFF box on fuel flow stays until the engine lights. The JFS shuts down on its own.
  4. Generators: nothing to do. Both switches are already on, and each generator comes online by itself as its engine spools up (the L GEN / R GEN cautions clear). Do not press ELEC - Left generator ON / OFF or ELEC - Right generator ON / OFF here: that switches them off. Reset the master caution with WARN - Master caution reset.
  5. Align the INS (next picture). Do not taxi while it aligns; moving restarts it.
  1. INS mode buttons: OFF, SH (stored heading, fast), GC (gyrocompass, slow), NAV, IFA. The chosen one is boxed.
  2. The alignment state: SH OK, GC with a countdown, then NAV.
  3. Alignment quality number.
  4. Whether a stored heading is held.
  5. GPS aiding on or off (yellow = off).
  6. Yellow SELECT NAV: alignment is done, press NAV.
  7. GPS button: turns GPS aiding on or off.
  8. HSI button: go back to the HSI.
  • SH (stored heading) takes about 40 seconds. Use it only if the jet has not moved since the last alignment.
  • GC (gyrocompass) takes about 4 minutes and always works.
  • When the state reads OK and the yellow SELECT NAV appears, touch NAV. Steerpoints only work in NAV.
  • You can reopen the INS page later from the page menu (M, then M2, then INS).
Tip. The HUD also shows the state of the alignment. On the ground it shows messages such as ALIGN, and NWS when nosewheel steering is on.
Part · Flying

How the jet behaves, from take-off to landing.

4. Flying it

Fly-by-wire

The jet's controls are fly-by-wire. Pull the stick to its stop and the jet gives you as much as it safely can: up to 9 G or the angle-of-attack limit (30°; 25° with CFTs), whichever comes first. You cannot over-G it, and it resists departing. The stick asks for a G, not a surface position.

  • Wings level: in the air, with the stick centred and less than 10° of bank, the jet rolls wings level and holds it. This also trims out a pull to one side from damage or an uneven load.
  • Uneven loads (for example one wing tank) are balanced by the flight controls: the jet rolls straight on take-off and in flight.
  • At high angle of attack the roll stick rolls the jet about its flight path without sideslip; use the rudder pedals if you want sideslip. Full-stick rolls at the AoA limit are slower than at low AoA.

Take-off

  • Run to about 160 knots (a heavy jet rotates later: around 34 tonnes, about 170 knots). With the stick centred the jet rotates by itself (10°, or 12° when heavy) and after lift-off holds that climb attitude for about 10 seconds; you can also rotate by hand. Once airborne with the stick centred it keeps the wings level.
  • Do not let the wheels roll faster than 230 knots ground speed: a tyre bursts and a TIRE caution shows.

Nosewheel steering and taxi

  • One button does it all: NWS button: tap = steering on / off, hold = manoeuvring range (45 deg). Tap it to switch steering on or off; hold it for the 45° manoeuvring range (tight parking spots) and let go to return to normal steering.
  • Nose Wheel Steering on / off is a plain on / off.
  • The HUD shows NWS when steering is on and NWS HI while the 45° range is held; nothing when it is off or you are airborne.
  • After a turn on the pedals the nose stays where you left it (it does not swing back).
  • The gear takes bumps, grass and pivot turns at walking pace without damage.

Landing

  • Put the flight path marker on the runway, flare normally, and lower the nose. With the stick centred after touchdown the nose comes down gently (about 1.5° a second), and a skip is settled.
  • The gear, dampers and brakes are modelled from scratch: the brakes are strong; a firm, heavy landing does not damage the gear, but a very hard one can.
  • Gear and doors follow the real sequence: the doors open, the gear moves, the doors shut again (also with the gear down).

Fuel and range

  • The F-15EX carries 13,550 lb internal. With CFTs (the F-15EX (CFTs) and the F-15IA) 23,305 lb.
  • The ENG page shows range and endurance at the present fuel flow. Set the bingo level there or with WARN - Bingo +500 lb / WARN - Bingo -500 lb; you get a call and a caution when you drop below it.
  • Drop tanks with WEAPONS - Jettison fuel tanks.

The three jets

JetNotes
F-15EXNo CFTs. 13,550 lb internal. 30° AoA limit.
F-15EX (CFTs)With conformal tanks. 23,305 lb. 25° AoA limit. The CFT tanks show on the fuel display.
F-15IAExport variant on the same avionics, with CFTs.

AI-flown F-15EX jets are limited the same way: 9 G, about Mach 2.5 at altitude.

Note. If you eject, the canopy is jettisoned first.
Part · Cockpit

The displays and how to drive them.

5. The cockpit at a glance

Five displays matter:

DisplayWhereWhat it is for
HUDGlass in front of youFlying (speed, altitude, heading, attitude) and aiming (target box, missile steering, gun).
HMD (helmet display)On your visor, follows your headThe HUD's main numbers wherever you look, plus a box on the target you have selected. Used to aim the AIM-9X.
LAD (large area display)The big touchscreen in the middle of the panelRadar, weapons, RWR, navigation, systems. You split it into windows and pick a page for each window.
EMD (engine / fuel display)Right side of the panel, two screensEngines, hydraulics and fuel.
RSD (standby display)Small square, low left of the LADBackup attitude, speed and altitude.
  1. Status strip along the top: clock, CAUTION, A/P, radios, IFF, navigation and so on. Many tiles are buttons.
  2. The window in command has the blue dotted frame. It gets your cursor and radar inputs.
  3. Small left windows (this layout shows ARMT stores and the FCS page).
  4. Small right windows (SIT-P and HSI here).
  5. M at the lower right corner of each window opens the page menu.
  6. The big middle window: here the radar ATTACK page.

Using the LAD (the touchscreen)

  • The mouse is your finger. Click a window to give it command (the blue dotted frame). The window in command receives the TDC and TMS inputs.
  • Double-click a window to move it to its next page.
  • M (lower right of each window) opens the page menu. Click a page name to open it. M2 switches to the second menu, M3 back to the first.
  • The top-right corner of a window opens the layout menu: 2 windows (left or right large), 4, 5, 7 or 8 windows. The default is 5. DISPLAYS - LAD next layout steps through them.
  • Status strip tiles are buttons (table below).

The castle switch

With a joystick, the castle switch does the touchscreen's job:

ControlShort pressHold 1 second
DISPLAYS - Castle left: short left window in command, hold 1 s next formatLeft window takes commandLeft window steps to its next page
DISPLAYS - Castle down: short middle window in command, hold 1 s next formatMiddle window takes commandMiddle window steps to its next page
DISPLAYS - Castle right: short right window in command, hold 1 s next formatRight window takes commandRight window steps to its next page
DISPLAYS - Castle forward: HUD in commandThe HUD takes command (a small star appears on the HUD)

DISPLAYS - LAD left window - next format, DISPLAYS - LAD middle window - next format and DISPLAYS - LAD right window - next format step a window's page directly.

6. The HUD

The HUD is green on the glass in front of you. It shows few things, but each one matters. The picture below is the normal flying HUD, in the NAV master mode with a steerpoint selected.

  1. Heading tape. The numbers are compass degrees (30 = 300), the ^ under the middle is the heading you are flying.
  2. Steerpoint bearing: the short bar under the tape is where the active steerpoint lies. Turn until it sits under the ^.
  3. Pitch ladder, one rung every 5 degrees. Solid rungs = nose above the horizon, dashed = below. The little ticks on the rung ends point toward the horizon.
  4. Horizon line (the long line with its ends turned down). It tilts with your bank.
  5. Flight path marker (circle with wings and a fin): where the jet is actually going. Put it on the horizon for level flight, on the runway for landing.
  6. Gun cross (+): the line your cannon points along. In the F-15EX it does not move; it marks the nose.
  7. Airspeed box: calibrated airspeed in knots.
  8. alpha (angle of attack) in degrees. The FBW limits you to 30 degrees (25 on the CFT jets).
  9. Altitude box, feet above sea level. The box has 4 digits below 10,000 ft and 5 above.
  10. Vertical speed in feet per minute (here 180 = climbing 180 ft/min).
  11. R = radar altitude: height above the ground in feet.
  12. Weapon block. Line 1 = selected weapon and how many are left (or gun rounds). Line 2 = Mach. Line 3 = G now and the highest G you pulled. SAFE appears above it while master arm is off.
  13. Steerpoint diamond: where the active steerpoint is. At the edge of the glass with an X through it when it is off to the side.
  14. Steerpoint range in nautical miles (N 24.6 = steerpoint 24.6 nm away).

Master modes: A/A and NAV

The jet starts in NAV. MASTER MODE - A/A selects A/A (air-to-air): all the attack symbols (range scale, shoot cue, steering circle...) show. Any weapon select also puts you in A/A. MASTER MODE - NAV goes back to NAV: the attack symbols are hidden and the steerpoint information is shown (steerpoint number, range and time to go). You can still fire weapons in NAV. MASTER MODE - Cycle A/A / NAV toggles between the two.

Shooting a radar missile (A/A mode)

  1. TD box (target designator): sits on the target the radar has picked. Solid = radar track, dotted = datalink track. At the edge of the glass it flashes with the angle off the nose.
  2. Shoot cue (six-point star): the missile you selected can be fired at this target now.
  3. ASE circle (dashed): the allowable steering error. Fly the steering dot inside it and the shot is good. The bigger the circle, the more forgiving the shot.
  4. Steering dot: where your flight path is relative to the best launch heading. Put it in the circle.
  5. Range scale line. The number on top is the radar range scale in nm (40).
  6. Target range caret (the triangle on the line) with the closure speed in knots next to it (1183).
  7. Launch zone cues on the line, from far to near: hollow triangle = Raero, hollow circle = Ropt, thick bar = Rpi, tee = Rmnvr, short bar = Rtr, foot = Rmin. See the table in chapter 6.
  8. Time to impact estimate before you shoot (T38 = 38 seconds). After the launch it becomes the countdown above the target box.
  9. Target block: its altitude in thousands of feet and its aspect (how far off its tail it points, and to which side), then its range in nm.
  10. Weapon line: the selected weapon (A C-7 10 = AIM-120C-7, 10 aboard).

The launch zone cues, from far to near

Symbol on the range lineNameMeaning in plain words
Hollow triangleRaeroThe farthest the missile can reach a target that does not run.
Hollow circleRoptThe best range to shoot: the target will have a hard time escaping.
Thick barRpiThe range inside which the target has little chance to defeat the missile.
Tee (sideways golf tee)RmnvrInside this the target can no longer out-turn the missile.
Short bar and tickRtrToo close to guide properly.
Foot with lineRminAbsolute minimum range.

The target caret and its closure speed number slide along the line as the range changes. A cue that would be above the top of the scale is hidden.

The dashed steering circle (ASE) grows as the target comes into range: it starts at 1.5 times Raero and is full size at Raero. With no medium-range missile on the jet, MRM shows no launch zone, circle or shoot cue.

After you shoot

Before the missile is active the text reads A12 (12 seconds until it goes active), then ACT flashes in a box, then a T35 style countdown to impact. These are the jet's own estimates.

Target off to the side

Short-range missile (AIM-9X)

WEAPONS - AIM-9X uncage / cage uncages the seeker. When the missile sees a target it growls (the tone) and the circle grows. With the helmet, look at the bandit and the circle follows; fire when the tone is steady. If you have a radar lock and the missile is caged, the circle follows the radar target.

Close-in radar modes (ACM)

For a dogfight the radar can search a small volume and lock the first target it sees. Hold RADAR - TMS up (DT / STT; hold 0.5 s: ACM SS; in ACM: SS / BST, hold LR BST) for half a second: that enters the ACM layer in SS. In the layer:

ControlACM mode
TMS up (short)SS or BST
TMS up (held)LR BST
TMS rightVTS
TMS leftLook at the target and lock it with the helmet
TMS downLeave ACM

The auto-acquisition controls do the same from outside the layer: RADAR - Auto acq forward: SS / BST, hold 1 s LR BST, RADAR - Auto acq aft: VTS and RADAR - Auto acq depress: return to search. ACM scans relative to the aircraft, so a bandit high above you in a hard turn is found.

Gun

Fire with WEAPONS - Gun trigger (fires the gun, any weapon selected). With the gun selected and a lock inside 12,000 ft the HUD shows a reticle with a range bar: the bar starts at 12 o'clock for 12,000 ft and unwinds clockwise as the range closes. Put the reticle on the target and fire. If the reticle blinks at the bottom edge of the HUD, the aim point is below the glass: pull more before firing. Without a range, the funnel and three search pips show.

SymbolMeaning
Dashed funnel, two sidesWhere your bullets will be if you keep your present turn.
Reticle with range barThe aiming point once the radar has a range.
Small star above the weapon blockThe HUD is in command (it receives the TDC and TMS inputs).

Ground warnings on the HUD

PULL UP and OBSTACLE appear low in the middle of the HUD. What they mean is in chapter 10.

7. The helmet display (HMD)

The HMD repeats the HUD's key symbols wherever you look. It needs the hook file Scripts\Hooks\F15EX_HMD_hook.lua; without it the symbols stay fixed to the nose. The symbols are placed at render time, so they stay locked on the point in the world as you move your head, in every direction round the jet.

  1. Heading tape for where you are LOOKING (not the nose).
  2. The aiming cross sits on your line of sight.
  3. Airspeed and angle of attack, the same as the HUD.
  4. Altitude, vertical speed and radar altitude, the same as the HUD.
  5. TD box and shoot cue on the target the radar has designated, drawn where the target really is.
  6. Range scale with caret and launch zone cues, as on the HUD.
  7. Small circles are other radar tracks in your field of view.
  8. Weapon block.
  9. Target block.

When the target is out of view

Incoming missile

An incoming missile is drawn in red (a ring with an M, spikes and a time to impact). If it is outside your view, a red triple chevron at the edge points to it. The rest of the HMD keeps its colour. A boxed MSL nn shows under the cross.

Steerpoint on the HMD

When a steerpoint is selected, the helmet display draws a diamond on it wherever you look (also behind you). If it is outside your view the diamond sits at the edge of the field toward it, with an X through it. Under the heading tape a bearing mark shows the steerpoint's bearing; past the end of the tape it stays pinned at the end with the bearing number under it.

Helmet controls

WhatControl name
Look at a target and lock itRADAR - HMD look and lock
9X uncage / cageWEAPONS - AIM-9X uncage / cage
Night vision goggles on / offNVG - Goggles on / off
Goggle gain upNVG - Gain up
Goggle gain downNVG - Gain down

HUD PROG: colours, brightness, HMD, goggles, night

ButtonDoes
HUD COLSteps the HUD symbol colour: green, white, yellow, cyan, amber. The sample symbol at the bottom shows it.
HMD COLThe same for the helmet display. Missile warnings stay red.
BRT UP / BRT DOWNHUD brightness in 10 % steps (10 to 100 %). Day and night each keep their own level: day starts at 100 %, night at 10 %. The helmet display follows.
HMDON / OFF. Off: no helmet symbols, and the radar's helmet look and the 9X cue fall back to the nose.
NVGNight vision goggles on / off, the same as NVG - Goggles on / off.
MODEDAY / NIGHT: dims the displays; the HUD and HMD keep their chosen colour. The same as DISPLAYS - Day / night mode.

At night, IFF colours (yellow / green / red), datalink identities and RWR threat colours stay coloured. These settings are not kept between flights: every spawn starts green, HMD on, day.

Part · Fighting

Find, identify, track, shoot, and defend yourself.

8. Radar, IFF, datalink and weapons

The radar is an AESA with one combined picture (no separate RWS and TWS modes): it shows tracks and also detections that have no track yet. You steer it with a cursor (the TDC) and the TMS switch.

  1. Radar range scale in nm (80). Change it with RADAR - Range scale up / down or by pushing the cursor past the top or bottom of the fan.
  2. Bearing and range of the cursor from you (322-36 = bearing 322, 36 nm).
  3. DCL (declutter) label.
  4. You: the cross at the bottom of the fan. The picture always points up, along your nose.
  5. Scan limit lines: the radar searches between them. They move with the cursor, or centre on the designated target.
  6. A track: hollow square. The stick shows which way it flies (longer = faster). The number is its place on your priority list. Yellow = not interrogated.
  7. Designated target (DT): dashed brackets, a cyan line to it and a small wedge on top.
  8. Green square = friend (IFF reply). Red = no IFF reply. Yellow = not asked.
  9. The cursor: two short vertical bars. Slew it with the TDC. The numbers beside it (31 over 08) are the altitude coverage at its range, in thousands of feet.
  10. Red circle with a ring: a ground or ship radar the RWR found.
  11. A circle round a track = the radar has an STT lock on it.
  12. Small dark bricks are raw radar detections that have no track yet.
  13. Altitude coverage scale: the radar's up-down coverage at the cursor range. The caret is your own altitude, the small yellow square is the target's.
  14. Designated target block: its altitude, ground speed, aspect and heading.
  15. Target bearing and range, and its closure speed under it.
  16. Missile zone scale: the dashed line shows the missile's reach against the target range.
  17. Touch labels. RDR switches the radar on and off (boxed = radiating).

Radar controls

Think of it like an F-16 radar: the cursor chooses where to look, TMS up picks and locks.

Do thisWhat happens
Move the TDC (cursor)The cursor moves on the ATTACK page. The bearing-range readout top left follows it. Push it past the top or bottom of the fan to change the range scale. Push it to the sides and the scan swings that way.
TMS up with the cursor on a trackThat track becomes the designated target (DT). The TD box appears on the HUD.
TMS up again on the DTSTT (single target track): the radar locks it. The target's warning receiver hears the lock. A circle is drawn round the track. Only works when the radar can really hold it ("NOT LOCKABLE" flashes if not). In STT the page shows only the locked target and datalink tracks.
TMS downBack from STT to the search picture. Again: drop the DT. Again: clear the priority list.
TMS rightStep the DT to the next track (your priority list first, then by range).
TMS leftAdd or remove the track under the cursor on your priority list (the small numbers 1 to 4 by the squares).
Hold TMS upEnter the ACM layer (chapter 6).
Antenna elevation up / downTilt the radar; hold the control for a smooth move. The caret on the altitude scale shows where it looks. With a DT the radar follows it automatically.
Scan width and barsA6 / A3 / A1 = scan width ±60 / ±30 / ±10°; 4B / 2B / 1B = bars. A narrower scan reaches farther.
EXPMagnifies the area round the DT (see below).
Radar powerSwitches the radar on or off. The page says RADAR OFF across the fan while it is off.

Category RADAR

WhatControl name
TDC up / down / left / right (hold)RADAR - TDC up (hold), RADAR - TDC down (hold), RADAR - TDC left (hold), RADAR - TDC right (hold)
TMS upRADAR - TMS up (DT / STT; hold 0.5 s: ACM SS; in ACM: SS / BST, hold LR BST)
TMS downRADAR - TMS down (back out; in ACM: leave ACM)

TMS rightRADAR - TMS right (next DT; in ACM: VTS)

Tip. Slew the cursor with a joystick axis or hold a TDC control for a constant rate.

The EXP inset

EXP opens a small window under and to the right of your aircraft on ATTACK, with the area round the DT magnified x2 or x4. It separates two aircraft flying in close formation so you can pick one. The DT line and the dotted line of a missile you fired show in EXP too, on ATTACK and on SIT-P.

What the radar can see

  • Range: about 145 nm on a 1 m² target, farther on larger aircraft (an AWACS out to the horizon). Range scales go up to 640 nm.
  • Stealthy aircraft are only seen at short range (an F-22 at about 27 nm).
  • Looking down over land the radar must pick the target out of the ground returns, so the range is shorter than looking up. The radar chooses high or medium pulse rate by itself.
  • NCTR (the type call) works on tracked targets without an STT, a few at a time. Its range depends on the target's size: full quality out to about 80 nm on a 5 m² target, about 54 nm on a 1 m² one, farther on big aircraft. Inside the limit you get the type, a little farther a class, beyond that UNK.
  • STT holds a target down to about 60 m and up to 60° off the nose in elevation.
  • Drones and cruise missiles (Shaheds and similar) show as ordinary radar tracks without a lock key. Air-to-air missiles and SAMs never do.

Your radar is quiet (LPI)

Other aircraft's radar warning receivers do not see your radar searching, in single player or multiplayer. A lock (STT) warns the target as normal, and so does a missile's own radar when it goes active.

IFF: who is who

Your interrogator asks each radar track who it is, about one second after it appears on the fan, out to 300 nm. Tracks turn green (friend), red (no reply: treat as hostile) or stay yellow (unknown). With the interrogator off every track is yellow. The IFF page sets it up:

ButtonDoes
M1, M2, M3, M4, MC (left)Your transponder modes on / off (a star marks the ones that are on). M4 steps A / B / OUT. MC is mode C (altitude).
M1 CODE, M2 CODE, M3 CODE (bottom)Open the KEY PAD on that code. Codes are octal (digits 0 to 7); M1's second digit is at most 3. A wrong code shows ERROR and is not taken.
MASTERTransponder master: NORM, LOW or EMER (emergency, shown amber).
I/PIdentify: your transponder flashes its identity for 18 seconds (count-down shown).
AAI (right)Your interrogator on / off (the same as the strip's IFF tile).
AUTO IDWhich tracks are asked automatically: ALL tracks, only the DT (and an STT target), or MAN (none until you press INTG).
INTGAsk now: interrogates the tracks AUTO ID allows (in MAN: all of them, once).

The middle shows your codes, the counts of FRIEND / NO REPLY / UNK, and a list of tracks with their answer, range and bearing.

Datalink tracks

Friendly AWACS, ground radars and other fighters send you tracks over Link 16. They appear next to your own radar tracks with a different symbol: a red chevron (hostile), a green dome (friend) and a yellow open box (unknown). A bar under a radar square means the datalink also reports that target. A dotted TD box on the HUD means you are aiming at a datalink track, not your own radar track. Friendly aircraft on the datalink show their type (F-16C and so on).

You can designate and shoot a hostile datalink track like a radar track, even with your radar off: the missile is guided on the datalink's data until its own radar goes active.

ItemMeaning
TERM LOADGO when the terminal is loaded.
NET ENTRYNetwork sync: COARSE SYNC, then FINE SYNC when tracks are flowing.
TXRECEIVE ONLY: the jet receives the network's tracks but does not send its own.
PPLI, SURV, F2FHow many tracks of each kind arrive: friendly positions, surveillance tracks (AWACS, ground radars), fighter-to-fighter tracks.
FRD, HOS, UNKHow many are friend, hostile, unknown.
Track listTrack number, identity, source, bearing, range, altitude and age of each track.
SHOW (left)Filter the list: ALL, FRND, HOST, UNK.
NPG (left)Filter by kind: ALL, PPLI, SURV, F2F.
SIT-P (right)Opens SIT-P in this window.

Weapons: the ARMT page

  1. Gun rounds left.
  2. Chaff and flare counts.
  3. Wing pylons (PYLN = empty). SRM / 9X x2 = two AIM-9X on the wing rail.
  4. Short-range missile stations.
  5. Missile stations. STBY = standing by, RDY = the selected one is ready. Under it the missile type (120D-3, 120C-7 ...).
  6. The selected station is a filled green box.
  7. Master arm: green ARM box when armed, white SAFE otherwise.
  8. COOL: the AIM-9X seeker is being cooled (boxed when it is).
  9. The weapon you have selected and how many are on board, in the cyan box.
  10. FUEL / tank state.

Category WEAPONS (EX)

WhatControl name
Select GUN / SRM / MRMWEAPONS - Weapon select GUN, WEAPONS - Weapon select SRM, WEAPONS - Weapon select MRM
Cycle weaponWEAPONS - Weapon select cycle
Master armWEAPONS - Master arm ARM / SAFE
Fire a missileWEAPONS - Weapon release (selected station)
Gun triggerWEAPONS - Gun trigger (fires the gun, any weapon selected)
AIM-9X uncage / cageWEAPONS - AIM-9X uncage / cage

Master mode A/A / NAVMASTER MODE - A/A, MASTER MODE - NAV, MASTER MODE - Cycle A/A / NAV

Step by step: an AIM-120 shot

  1. MASTER MODE - A/A, then WEAPONS - Weapon select MRM. Turn on master arm. The ARMT page shows a green ARM box.
  2. Put the cursor on a radar track and press TMS up. The TD box appears on the HUD.
  3. Watch the range scale. When the caret is between the triangle (Raero) and the bar (Rpi), the shoot cue (star) appears.
  4. Fly the steering dot into the dashed circle (ASE).
  5. Fire with WEAPONS - Weapon release (selected station). The missile does not need a lock to be fired at a designated target. Keep the target in the radar's view: your radar guides the missile until its own radar goes active (the A / ACT countdown). The dotted line to the target shows while the missile is still guiding.
  6. After ACT you can turn away: the missile is on its own.

The missile countdown (TTI / TTA)

About a second after a launch, a T number appears on the ATTACK page's missile line (and on the HUD): seconds to impact. A shows seconds to the seeker going active, then turns into ACT. Two digits, three past 99 seconds. The number counts down one second a second and does not jump: it is a lead-collision estimate from the round's own measured speed and its expected slowing, and the display is smoothed, so a loft or a turning target changes the rate, not the number. ACT means the seeker is active and guiding itself.

Weapons available

WeaponType
AIM-120C-5, C-7, C-8, D, D-3Medium-range radar missiles, all available together
AIM-174B, AIM-260ALong-range radar missiles
AIM-200A (Peregrine)Small radar missile, four to a BRU-61C on the CFT's aft pylon
AIM-9XShort range, high off-boresight, aimed with the helmet
Python-5 (F-15IA)Short range, infrared
APKWS rockets (x21 on pylons 2 and 14)Short-range, infrared, against drones; counted as SRM (code APK)
M61 gunCannon (choose the ammunition belt in the mission editor)

The mission editor has 15 single stations, so you can load each wing rail and fuselage / CFT station on its own, and 26 presets for each variant.

Other air-to-air missiles. To use an air-to-air missile the mission editor does not list (ED's own, a module's or a weapon mod's), add its CLSID to the pylon's launcher list in F15EX.lua (and in F15EX_CFT.lua / F15IA.lua if you fly those), then restart DCS. The ARMT page reads the missile's data and sorts it: infrared = SRM, active radar = MRM, semi-active = MRM that needs an STT (the page says NO STT). The HUD weapon line shows the family letter, the count and a short code (for example S2 R-73). A missile with a body larger than an AMRAAM may not sit perfectly on the rail. Missiles from mods that load after the F-15EX are not listed.

9. Defence: RWR, situation page, chaff and flares

EW-P: the RWR page

This shows who is looking at you or shooting at you. Heading is up.

  1. You: the broken cross in the middle.
  2. The 12 dots on the clock. Threats close to the centre are strong (close or dangerous), far out are weak.
  3. Compass rose that turns with your heading. N, E, S, W and 3, 6, 12 ... 33 are compass marks.
  4. Triangle = an airborne radar. The number is its code (29 = MiG-29). A circle round it = it has locked you.
  5. Circle with a boat line = a ship radar (49 here).
  6. 50 = a long-range search radar (AWACS type). These never appear in the inner ring.
  7. Numbers 10 / 11 etc. = surface-to-air missile radars (SA-10 / SA-11 style codes).
  8. CHF and FLR: chaff and flares left.
  9. CMD: the countermeasure mode. Press the CMD button for the programs page.
  10. PWR (top left): how far from the centre a threat is drawn = how strong its signal is. If you switch on the range scale, this label changes and threats are placed by their estimated range.
  11. Number of emitters the RWR is hearing (5 EMTR).

How to read a threat

  • The number is the radar type (29 = MiG-29, 10 = SA-10, 11 = SA-11, 50 = a search radar).
  • Its direction is the direction to the threat; its distance from the middle is the signal strength (inner = strong).
  • Triangle round the number = airborne radar. Boat line under it = ship.
  • Circle round it = it has locked you.
  • If a missile is guided toward you, the triangle (air) or circle (ground) flashes. At the top centre you also get LAUNCH, or MSL ACT with seconds to impact.
  • You also hear tones (different tones for search, lock and launch).

SIT-P: the situation page

SIT-P puts radar tracks, RWR emitters, datalink tracks, your route and the bullseye on one round map.

  1. Range ring. The ring's top edge is the range shown top right (80 nm).
  2. You (cyan cross). Heading up.
  3. Yellow line with arrow: your heading.
  4. Designated target: magenta brackets and a cyan line from you. Magenta brackets also mean that radar has locked or launched on you.
  5. A radar track: square with a stick and its altitude in thousands of feet.
  6. Orange triangle = an RWR emitter that is searching. Red = it is locking or has launched.
  7. Red triangle with magenta brackets: a threat that has locked you.
  8. White triangle: an air radar emitter with the number of its type.
  9. N / E / S / W on the ring.
  10. Filter buttons down the left: LNE (route line), AIR, GND, SAM, FTF. A green box = on.
  11. JTID: show datalink tracks from friendly fighters / AWACS.
  12. Range scale.
  13. Legends for the bottom row.
  • DCTR (right side, button 14) moves your own aircraft to the centre of the ring, so you see all round you.
  • Radar tracks take the IFF colours (green / red / yellow) as on ATTACK.
  • The NCTR call (class, then type) shows low right of the track under the TDC and of the DT; friendly datalink aircraft show their type.
  • A SAM site the RWR has located stays on the map for the rest of the mission.

Category TEWS (EX)

WhatControl name
SIT-P range scaleSIT-P - Range scale
Show / hide radar tracksSIT-P - Filter AIR (radar tracks)
Show / hide SAMs and shipsSIT-P - Filter SAM (RWR ground / ship emitters)
Show / hide datalink tracksSIT-P - Filter JTID (datalink tracks)
EW-P scaleTEWS - Scale PWR / 40 / 80 / 160 nm

Countermeasures: chaff and flares

  • One press of the chaff or flare control drops one. The jet carries 120 chaff and 120 flares by default.
  • Programs drop a series automatically. MAN 1 runs the manual program (8 chaff + 8 flares in two bursts). MAN 2 runs its own program, or in SEMI the program for the threat that is attacking you (air or SAM).
  • The mode has five positions: OFF, STBY, MAN, SEMI, AUTO. In AUTO the jet runs the right program by itself when it sees a launch.
  • The select switch picks CHAFF, BOTH or FLARE for the manual programs.
  • Nothing drops on the ground.
  • There is no ECM jammer: defence is the RWR, chaff, flares and manoeuvre.

Category WEAPONS (EX)

WhatControl name
Chaff, oneWEAPONS - Chaff (one)
Flare, oneWEAPONS - Flare (one)
Program MAN 1CMD - MAN 1 program
Program MAN 2CMD - MAN 2 program (threat program in SEMI / AUTO)
Mode OFF-STBY-MAN-SEMI-AUTOCMD - Mode OFF / STBY / MAN / SEMI / AUTO
Select CHAFF-BOTH-FLARECMD - Dispense select CHAFF / BOTH / FLARE

Editing the programs

On the EW-P page, touch the CMD button to open the program editor own design. Every program and option is editable.

  1. Program buttons: MAN1, MAN2, AIR, SAM, and DFLT to put the chosen program back to its default.
  2. The program you are editing.
  3. Its settings: chaff and flares per salvo, how many salvos, the gap between salvos, bursts, the gap between bursts.
  4. The row with the green box is selected. Use - / + to change it or KEY PAD to type a number.
  5. Totals: how much chaff and flare the program drops and how long it takes.
  6. Options: auto repeat, the minimum level warning, auto on lock.
  7. MODE (OFF / STBY / MAN / SEMI / AUTO) and SEL (CHAFF / BOTH / FLARE).
  8. - and + change the selected row.
  9. UP / DN move the selected row; RTN goes back to EW-P.
Note. Chaff and flares come from the jet's real inventory. When either is at 20 or fewer, the MINIMUM light comes on.
Part · Systems and navigation

Engines, fuel, warnings, lights, steerpoints, terrain following, autopilot and radios.

10. Flight and systems pages, warnings and lights

Engine / fuel display (EMD)

The EMD has two screens in one framed panel. The upper one shows the radios (R1 and R2, OFF or the frequency) and the engines; an engine that is not running shows an amber OFF box instead of its RPM and fuel flow. The lower one shows the hydraulics (a box turns amber below 1,500 psi) and fuel: total, the wing, fuselage and, on the CFT jets, conformal tanks, and the bingo. It runs from the battery, so you can watch the start on it.

  1. R1 and R2: the two radios (frequency and channel; dashes when off).
  2. RPM in percent, left engine on the left, right engine on the right.
  3. Turbine temperature in degrees C.
  4. Fuel flow in pounds per hour.
  5. Nozzle position dials: needle at 0 = nozzle closed (idle / mil), 100 = fully open (afterburner).
  6. Oil pressure in psi.
  1. Hydraulic pressures: PC1, UTIL, PC2. Pointer in the green band = good.
  2. TOTAL fuel in pounds.
  3. INT = internal fuel only (the rest is in external tanks).
  4. Fuel tank shapes fill from the bottom. The middle one is the main tank, the sides are wings.

At night the amber boxes become amber outlines with the text on black, so they stay readable.

The pages on the LAD

ADI: the attitude page

  1. Heading tape with a green caret.
  2. Airspeed box with angle of attack under it.
  3. Altitude box with vertical speed under it.
  4. Attitude ball: blue = sky, yellow = ground. The white numbers are pitch in degrees.
  5. The fixed reference marks: line them up like a toy aeroplane on the horizon.
  6. Bank scale along the bottom: ticks at 10, 20, 30, 45, 60 degrees.
  7. Bank pointer.
  8. Turn rate: the green triangle sits on a bracket, one standard turn at the inner tick.
  9. Slip ball: keep it in the middle (coordinated flight).
  10. PT arrows: raise or lower the little reference aeroplane (pitch trim of the display).

ENG: engine numbers, bingo and LAW

The same numbers as the EMD in text form, plus cruise data: range and endurance on the fuel you have at the present fuel flow, and END FUEL, the fuel you expect to have over the last steerpoint.

The ENG page is also where you set the bingo fuel and the LAW height:

ButtonDoes
BINGOOpens the KEY PAD on the bingo field (type a number, ENT)
BNG + / BNG -Bingo up / down in 500 lb steps
LAWOpens the KEY PAD on the LAW field (also on the KEY PAD's top row)
LAW + / LAW -Height up / down in 100 ft steps (switches LAW on)
LAW ON / OFFThe same as the LAW tile on the strip

The EMD's bottom line shows the bingo; the strip's LAW tile shows the height.

FCS: flight controls

For checking the fly-by-wire: where every surface is and whether each channel is healthy.

  1. Top line: ACE GN number, the DETAIL BIT label and the lateral asymmetry readout (how unbalanced the jet is left to right). These come from the real jet's page.
  2. Green squares = a working channel. A dash = a channel that is out.
  3. Pitch / roll / yaw trim, as a percentage of full trim.
  4. Each control surface has a red scale with a yellow marker showing where it is now: ailerons ...
  5. ... flaps ...
  6. ... stabilators ...
  7. ... and rudders (horizontal scale).
  8. L AOA / R AOA: the two angle-of-attack vanes.

BIT: systems and cautions

Both engines, the start state, generators, throttle position, hydraulics, batteries and buses, JFS, fuel and bingo, and the list of active cautions.

Cautions

A new caution lights the master caution (on the strip and the HUD) and, in the air, the warning voice calls it. Reset with WARN - Master caution reset or by touching the CAUTION tile.

CautionMeaning
L / R ENG, ENGINE OUT, ENGINE LIGHT-OFFEngine state
L / R FIREEngine fire
L / R GEN, BATTGenerator or battery problem
PC1 HYD, PC2 HYD, UTIL HYDLow hydraulic pressure
L / R OILLow oil pressure
FUEL LOW, BINGOTotal fuel is below the bingo level you set
LOW ALTBelow the LAW height (next section)

Ground warnings: LAW, PULL UP and OBSTACLE

Three warnings protect you near the ground. All three work only in the air with the gear up and the electrics on.

WarningWhenWhat you getSwitch
LAW (low altitude warning)You descend below the LAW height on the radar altimeter (500 ft unless you change it).LOW ALT caution and the low-altitude voice warning, played twice. It sounds again only after you climb back above 1.1 times the height and cross it again.LAW tile, ENG page
PULL UP (emergency)The jet works out that a normal recovery (rolling wings level, then pulling about 4 G) would only just clear the ground ahead. Works with or without the NAV pod.PULL UP on the HUD and the "pull up" voice. The cue and the voice always come together: the voice plays once when the cue appears, and the cue stays until you have been clear for 1.5 seconds. A new warning after that plays the voice again.GCWS tile
OBSTACLEOnly with the AAQ-13 NAV pod and the TF radar on (chapter 11): rising terrain ahead would need a pull of 2 G or more to clear.OBSTACLE on the HUD and the "obstacle ahead" voice, repeated while it lasts.Needs the NAV pod

PULL UP comes first: it interrupts any other call. The warnings use the ground (terrain) only, not buildings, trees or wires.

Auto GCAS

The strip's GCAS tile turns the automatic recovery on or off (on by default). When the jet predicts it will meet the ground, PULL UP comes first, then AUTO GCAS appears under it: the jet rolls the wings level the shortest way (an inverted jet rolls upright first) and pulls up (about 5 g, or the AoA limit) until it is climbing clear, then hands control back. The autopilot drops out. Take control back at any time with the paddle, a push or a roll past half stick. With the tile off there is no fly-up and no emergency PULL UP; the LAW warning still works. Level flight over flat ground or water does not trigger it; a dive, a sink or rising ground ahead does.

Voice warnings

Besides the ground warnings: the master caution voice for a new caution, engine fire (left / right), over-G, hydraulics, bingo, and fuel at 1,500 / 800 / 500 lb. There are no voice calls for missiles: the RWR tones warn you instead.

Exterior lights

The lights run from the AC generators (no light before the engines run; the gear light also goes out when the gear is up). Each change shows a message.

11. Navigation, terrain following and autopilot

HSI

The HSI is a compass rose with your heading up. The rose is also the range circle.

  1. AUTO SEQ: when boxed, the active steerpoint moves on automatically when you reach it.
  2. RNG: the HSI scale, with arrows to make it bigger or smaller.
  3. CMD HDG: the heading to fly for the steering you selected.
  4. Orange bug on the rose: the same CMD HDG, shown as a direction.
  5. Green double chevron: the TACAN station's bearing.
  6. Green circle: the TACAN station itself at its range.
  7. Cyan course pointer (line with a diamond): the course you set. The diamond slides sideways to show how far off the course you are.
  8. TACAN block: station, bearing / range, time to station.
  9. STR block: the steerpoint, bearing / range and the time left (E = en route).
  10. Tail of the bearing pointer: the reciprocal of the TACAN bearing.
  11. CRS: the course you set.
  12. Steering selector: TCN, ILST (ILS), GT, ILSN, NAV. The boxed one steers the jet.
  13. You in the middle of the rose. The rose turns so your heading is at the top.

Steering: what the jet steers to

The bottom row picks the steering source: TCN (TACAN), ILST (ILS), GT (ground track: the route's legs), RTE (the route with its altitudes, used by the autopilot), ILSN, NAV (steerpoints). The boxed one is active. The HUD, ADI and HSI show it.

Typing numbers: the KEY PAD

Touch the KEY PAD tile on the strip. Choose a field on the left buttons (TCN, ILS, CRS, STPT, HDG, R1, R2), type, then ENT. RTN goes back. TACAN band X / Y is a single touch. Pages such as ENG and IFF open the KEY PAD on their own fields.

Category NAV (EX)

WhatControl name
Next / previous steerpointNAV - Next steerpoint, NAV - Previous steerpoint
Steering source STPT / TCN / ILSNAV - Steering STPT / TCN / ILS
Steerpoint auto-sequencingNAV - Steerpoint auto-sequencing ON / OFF

TACAN bandTACAN - Band X / Y

Terrain following (TF)

The jet can follow the terrain at low level with the AAQ-13 NAV pod on the NAV pylon: its terrain-following radar looks ahead and the autopilot flies the climbs and descents. Without the pod there is no TF (the pages say NO NAV POD / NO POD).

  • The TF radar is OFF without the pod, in STBY on the ground or below 100 knots ground speed, and ON in the air above that. The strip's NF / TF tile shows the state.
  • The TF page shows what the radar sees and how the jet will fly over it. The autopilot's TF mode (A/P TF CPL on this page, or TF on the A/P page) flies it.
ItemMeaning
CLRSet clearance: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 or 1,000 ft. 500 ft is the default. 100 ft only in VLC; WX2 needs 500 ft or more.
RIDEHow hard the jet flies the terrain: SOFT, MED (default) or HARD (more G and steeper dives).
MODEThe radar mode: NORM, ECCM, WX1, WX2 (bad weather), LPI (quiet), VLC (very low clearance).
FREQThe radar's frequency channel.
A/P TF CPLCouples the autopilot to terrain following (boxed when coupled).
A/POpens the A/P page.
R and G numbersRadar altitude (ft) and ground speed (kt).
MEAMinimum safe altitude to the next steerpoint: the highest ground within 2 nm of the leg plus 1,000 ft.
PictureThe ground ahead (distance in nm along the bottom) and the line the jet will fly over it, against the horizontal clearance line. RAW / SYN = radar or synthetic video; ZCL = zero command line; OWL = obstacle warning line.
FLY UP, TF FAILThe TF cannot clear the ground ahead (climb now) / the TF has failed.

Autopilot

The autopilot is built on the fly-by-wire, so all the limits still apply. A/P - Engage / disengage (HDG / ATT by the bank; ALT, STR if selected) turns it on and off; A/P - Paddle: autopilot off always turns it off.

ModeHow you get it
A/P HDG: hold headingEngage with less than 7° of bank.
A/P ATT: hold attitudeEngage with 7 to 60° of bank. The jet keeps the bank and pitch.
A/P ALT: hold altitudeSelect ALT HOLD first (A/P - ALT HOLD select / deselect), then engage.
A/P NAV, AHDG: steeringSelect STR first (A/P - STR (couple to the HSI steering) select / deselect), then engage. The jet follows the steerpoint, TACAN, ILS or the selected heading, with at most 30° of bank. To a steerpoint, a TACAN radial or the ILS it corrects for the wind and stays on the line; in heading mode the wind drifts it (as intended).

It will not engage with weight on the wheels, with more than 60° of bank or 45° of pitch, or with the stick out of centre. A small roll input steers the jet without disconnecting it; let go and it holds the new heading. A big stick movement (pitch past a quarter or roll past 80 %) disconnects.

Vertical modes

Buttons 6 to 10 on the A/P page. One touch each; touching an active one again turns it off and leaves the autopilot on.

ButtonDoes
PATHHolds the climb or descent angle you have now. Level, it holds the altitude. The strip shows A/P PATH.
RTEFlies the route's legs with lead turns and climbs or descends to each steerpoint's altitude. Also on the HSI.
TFTerrain following at the TF page's clearance and ride. Needs the NAV pod: without it the page shows NO POD and refuses.
CLRSteps the TF clearance.
RIDESteps the TF ride.

A pitch stick movement disconnects the vertical mode. If the route command is lost the jet falls back to altitude hold. The GT and RTE buttons on the HSI choose the steering source.

Paddle (off)A/P - Paddle: autopilot off
ALT HOLDA/P - ALT HOLD select / deselect

12. Radios

The jet has two V/UHF radios: R1 and R2. They work with DCS's own communication menu (ATC, tankers, flight leads, AWACS), mission-editor presets and guard. Open the menu with Communications menu (category RADIOS (EX)).

  • Switch each radio on with R1 - Power on / off / R2 - Power on / off.
  • Change channel with R1 - Channel up / R1 - Channel down (and the same for R2), or type a channel (1 to 20) or a frequency in MHz in the KEY PAD (fields R1 and R2).
  • Guard: an extra receiver on the emergency frequency (R1 - Guard on / off, R2 - Guard on / off); a G after the frequency shows it is monitored.
  • Push to talk: PTT 1 - Mic switch forward: transmit on R1 (comm menu) and PTT 2 - Mic switch aft: transmit on R2 (comm menu).

The frequencies and channels also show on the EMD (top) and on the strip's R1 / R2 tiles.

COMM page

R1 on the left (PWR, RCV, GRD), R2 on the right; the middle shows each radio's frequency and channel. Receive off mutes everything that radio hears (for example the AWACS on R2) and the page says RCV OFF. The radio can still transmit, so a request is answered but you will not hear the reply. Radio volume is not adjustable.

14. What is not there

These are known and intended for this release. They are not faults.

ItemState
Air-to-ground weapons and sensorsNot part of this release: no A/G weapons, no A/G radar and no working targeting pod. The TGP and IRST pods can be fitted as stores but have no function. The AAQ-13 NAV pod provides terrain following and the OBSTACLE warning.
External aircraft modelNot shipped; the CFT app in the package's Tools folder installs the model you choose (chapter 2).
Menu pages that open an empty frame (TSD, TGT IR, A/G RDR, IRST, EVENT, PROG and the M2 entries listed in chapter 5)The system behind them is not built.
ECM jammingNot modelled. Defence is the RWR, chaff, flares and manoeuvre.
Datalink transmitThe jet receives Link 16 tracks but does not send its own.
Radio volume, interior cockpit lights, HF radioNot modelled. The HF, SSB tiles are legends only.
Friendly versus enemy SAM coloursSAM symbols show the threat state, not the side: DCS gives no coalition for a ground emitter.
Ground warningsTerrain only: no buildings, trees, towers or wires.
SoundsSome cockpit engine and JFS sounds use ED's stock ones.
HOTAS defaultsMost commands have none; bind them yourself (chapters 2 and 13).
Missiles from mods that load after the F-15EXNot listed in the mission editor (chapter 8).
Settings between flightsHUD PROG choices, IFF, LAW and bingo return to their defaults at every spawn.
